rounds.text: CLN Energy Ltd exhibits top-tier capital efficiency and explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion that significantly outpaces broader industry benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E14, E15]. Specifically, the company generates a robust ROCE of 22.35% and an ROE of 19.63%, easily beating their respective sector benchmarks of 12.77% and 11.38% [E9, E10]. This exceptional fundamental performance is paired with hyper-growth, demonstrated by compounded sales growth of 58% and compounded profit growth of 55% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a supportive macroeconomic backdrop within the Automobile & Auto Components sector, which carries a positive tailwind score [E45]. Valuation multiples also present a compelling entry point relative to peers, with an EV/EBITDA of 8.09x against a sector benchmark of 11.79x, and a P/E of 13.67x compared to a sector benchmark of 23.7x [E6, E11]. Conceded: cash conversion is negative at -2.19x and operating cash flow dropped to Rs -46 Cr in March 2026 alongside a rise in borrowings [E20, E21, E26].

CLN Energy Ltd trades at a demanding P/E of 25.4 [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 4.52x against a market price of ₹ 493 [E2], while offering a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation places intrinsic value at ₹ 452 per share, leaving a negative margin of safety of -9.0% [E32, E33], and the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already requires an 11.2% earnings growth rate to be justified [E34]. Operational health exhibits a severe disconnect from reported profitability, highlighted by negative operating cash flow of Rs -46 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -50 Cr in Mar 2026 [E20, E21, E22], which translates to a distressing cash conversion of -2.19x [E20]. This cash burn is accompanied by a massive surge in borrowings, which spiked to Rs 93 Cr in Mar 2026 from just Rs 16 Cr a year prior [E26], while operating margins remain inconsistent across yearly and quarterly periods [E18, E19]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing growth metrics including 58% sales growth and 55% profit growth alongside a high return on capital employed of 22.35% [E10, E14, E15].

Conceded: the share price trades above the scanX DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 452, resulting in a negative margin of safety [E32, E33], and dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4]. However, the bear's emphasis on a demanding P/E of 25.4 [E1] ignores a key provider metric placing the P/E at an attractive 13.67x against a sector benchmark of 23.7x [E6]. The concern over negative operating cash flow [E20, E21] is heavily outweighed by stellar fundamental efficiency, demonstrated by an ROE of 19.63% and ROCE of 22.35% that easily outpace sector benchmarks of 11.38% and 12.77% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the company's rapid scaling is evident in its 58% sales growth and 55% profit growth [E14, E15], alongside improving operational efficiency as working capital requirements dropped from 79.6 days to 63.2 days [E38]. Institutional backing remains exceptionally firm with positive money flow and stable 72.60% promoter and 12.60% foreign institutional holdings [E28, E29, E31]. Finally, profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 66%, proving that business fundamentals are outperforming recent market expectations and the automobile and auto components sector tailwind supports the setup [E36, E45].

Conceded: sector benchmarks place P/E at 13.67x [E6], ROE at 19.63% [E9], and ROCE at 22.35% [E10]. However, filed statements show a true P/E of 25.4 [E1] and price-to-book of 4.52x [E2], meaning valuation is significantly more demanding than alternate key-ratios suggest. The bull minimizes severe cash destruction by pointing to returns, but operating cash flow plunged to Rs -46 Cr alongside free cash flow of Rs -50 Cr in Mar 2026 [E21, E22], producing a cash conversion ratio of -2.19x [E20]. Furthermore, borrowings spiked from Rs 16 Cr to Rs 93 Cr in just one year [E26], invalidating the notion of a pristine balance sheet. While sales and profit growth reached 58% and 55% [E14, E15], the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends remain inconsistent [E18, E19]. Finally, despite strong institutional holdings [E28, E29], the stock trades at a negative margin of safety [E33] while offering a 0.00% dividend yield [E4].
